HONESTLY SCOPED, and the gate's own docstring is the authority: it sees Write, Edit and MultiEdit only. NotebookEdit is in its tool tuple but no matcher delivers it, so it is not covered. Bash and Codex sessions are not covered at all -- the R04 canonical-dirt alarm is the planned compensating control and is NOT BUILT YET, so those paths are uncompensated today. This control does not replace pr_only_main_ruleset; it binds EARLIER, at the edit, and that control still binds at merge.

load_layer_flip_owed: AT THE ENFORCEMENT FLIP, NOT BEFORE: eight rules whose `control` is session_boot move to a pack, so their delivery stops being the boot recitation — 25fcddee, 3fa17fa0, 72e06bdf, 113b3833, 57d13061, c66dc739, 49533583, 557838a5. Their control must change to the pack compiler in the SAME change that flips the mode, and not while shadow mode leaves recitation intact: claiming a control that is not yet carrying the rule is exactly what rule ab814a26 forbids.
load_layer_note: THE DELIVERY HALF of the enforcement recategorization (2026-08-23 rules council, both chairs unanimous). `rule_controls` above says HOW a rule is enforced; this says WHEN its text is delivered to a session. layer0 = recited at every boot, and nothing task-specific belongs here (rule 1fddcffb). control = an installed deny/stop/schema control prints the rule at the moment it binds, so boot recitation is belt-and-suspenders; ops/rule-load-layer-check.py REFUSES this value for any rule whose enforcement_class is not built, which is what stops 'scoped' from meaning 'silently dropped'. pack = delivered when the observed work matches a pack's triggers. A wildcard pack is refused by the same check: grok's warning was that shipping wildcard tags and calling it scoping is how rules go silent on an undeclared session.
